context: linear earthworks · excavation and lining by reach; structures in the dry; watering season fixes the dates

brief.intro: New to this project type? A canal project moves water across land by gravity through an excavated and lined channel, with structures along it that control and distribute the flow: head regulators, cross regulators, intakes to branch canals, siphons and aqueducts where the canal crosses a road, a drain or a river, and bridges for the roads that cross the canal. Most of the quantity is earthwork and lining, done reach by reach with a train of excavators, trimmers and lining crews. The structures are ordinary reinforced concrete, but they must be built 'in the dry', and when the work is on an existing canal that is only possible during the yearly closure when the water is shut off. Farmers need the water on a fixed date — the irrigation season, not the contractor, sets the deadline.

scope.name: Survey & setting out
scope.desc: Canal alignment, bed levels and cross-sections along the whole length.

scope.name: Excavation & embankment
scope.desc: Cutting the canal prism and building the banks to profile.

scope.name: Trimming & sub-grade preparation
scope.desc: Accurate trimming of bed and side slopes before lining.

scope.name: Canal lining
scope.desc: Concrete, shotcrete, geomembrane or masonry lining with joints.

scope.name: Head & cross regulators
scope.desc: Gated structures that control level and flow.

scope.name: Intakes & turnouts
scope.desc: Structures that deliver water to branch canals and fields.

scope.name: Siphons, aqueducts & culverts
scope.desc: Crossings under or over roads, drains and rivers.

scope.name: Bridges
scope.desc: Road and foot bridges over the canal.

scope.name: Gates & hoists
scope.desc: Steel gates, lifting gear and, often, remote operation.

scope.name: Service roads & drainage
scope.desc: Roads on the banks and drains alongside the canal.

scope.name: Watering test & handover
scope.desc: Filling the canal reach by reach, checking seepage and operating the gates.

the concrete or membrane surface that stops water seeping away and protects the banks.

a small gated outlet from the canal to a branch or a field channel.
a pipe or box that carries the canal under an obstacle and up again on the other side.

the yearly period when an existing canal is shut and dry, used for maintenance and construction.

must_get_right: Fix the dates of the watering season and the canal closure first — they are the deadlines. Work that needs a dry canal must fit entirely inside the closure.
Plan earthworks and lining as a production train per reach, with cubic metres and square metres per day, and balance cut against fill to limit haulage.
Structures control the reach: a reach cannot be watered until every regulator, siphon and turnout in it is complete and its gates are installed.
Gates and hoists are fabricated items with long lead; order them when the structure drawings are approved, not when the concrete is finished.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by canal reach (between structures) for earthworks and lining, and structure by structure, so each reach shows whether it can be watered.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar with the canal closure period and the irrigation season marked; earthworks productivity is reduced in the wet months.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Per reach: excavation and banks → trimming → lining; structures in the reach in parallel, built in the dry; gates after structures. A reach is watered when lining, structures and gates are all complete. On existing canals, in-canal work is tied to the closure start and finish.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Land is available along the alignment; the closure is granted on the published dates; borrow and disposal areas are approved; power is available at the regulators.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule tracks the following as milestones because they drive the programme:

rows: Embedded parts before second-stage concrete; gates before watering
Before lining of the first reach

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Long, narrow site with access only along the banks; high groundwater in the canal bed; work inside an existing canal limited to the closure.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: late land access, groundwater and soft ground, flooding of the works, late gates, and missing the closure window. Contingency is held before the watering date.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by canal reach and structure; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the earthworks, lining and structure crews — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
